accepted_units.title: Replace an inaccessible exact nerve by a computable flag complex without confusing the two
accepted_units.why_material: The exact Cech representation captures the union under a good-cover hypothesis but requires intersection or accurate-distance data, whereas the Rips representation is determined by pairwise observations and can introduce topology absent from the exact object. This is a reusable distinction between semantic fidelity and observability or computability.
accepted_units.context_note: The Cech theorem and historical Rips construction are cited background. The source uses them to formulate its own certificate; it does not claim that a single Rips complex generally recovers the covered region.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The conclusion depends on convex ball covers, Euclidean distance, the good-cover condition, and scale conventions; normalized Cech glyphs and inequalities should be verified before exact symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Sandwich an exact representation between observable approximations at two scales
accepted_units.why_material: The source proves that an unavailable Cech complex can be factored between Rips complexes at smaller and larger scales, with a sharp worst-case scale ratio. The proof reduces a common-intersection question to regular-simplex geometry and extends the finite-dimensional bound through Helly's theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a deterministic geometric theorem under Euclidean assumptions, not a probabilistic or simulation result. The exact dimension-dependent constant is materially damaged in normalization and must be read from the typeset source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The factorization depends on ambient dimension, Euclidean convexity, ball-radius conventions, and the precise scale inequality; exact constants and displayed algebra are unsafe from normalized text alone.

accepted_units.title: A local diameter condition certifies that the realized simplex stays inside the cover
accepted_units.why_material: A clique simplex is linked back to geometry by showing that every point of its convex hull is close enough to at least one vertex. This supplies the semantic bridge needed to turn combinatorial chains into statements about the union of cover sets.
accepted_units.context_note: The lemma is deterministic and conditional on the radius bound. Its proof uses the preceding simplex-geometry result; no random-placement assumption or empirical evidence is involved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The numerical bound is dimension dependent and glyph-damaged, and the bridge relies on Euclidean convex realization and radially symmetric coverage.

accepted_units.title: Demand persistence to reject scale-specific phantom witnesses
accepted_units.why_material: Nonzero relative homology at one observable scale can be a false witness of global coverage. Requiring the same class to remain nonzero under inclusion to a coarser scale filters classes that arise from representation artifacts and are filled in when additional relations become visible.
accepted_units.context_note: The illustrated two-dimensional configuration is explanatory rather than exhaustive. Persistence is used here as a sufficient filter inside a theorem with explicit geometric and boundary assumptions, not as a universal proof that every surviving class has the desired meaning.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The inference depends on tracking one class under the induced map between paired Rips and fence complexes; group ranks at the two scales alone do not encode the same information.

accepted_units.title: A null cycle in a bounded collar dies after a controlled scale increase
accepted_units.why_material: The lemma combines bounded collar thickness, a Rips-Cech factorization, the nerve theorem, and duality to show that a cycle trivial in the underlying shell becomes trivial in a larger-scale Rips complex. It is the geometric mechanism that prevents a boundary artifact from persisting indefinitely.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a conditional deterministic lemma. The proof uses a thickened hypersurface model and Alexander duality; the exact scale formula is extraction-damaged and should not be reused without the typeset source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The claim relies on the collar being a manifold-times-interval with bounded thickness, on Euclidean ball covers, and on the precise relation between the two scales.

accepted_units.title: A nonzero relative boundary degree obstructs an uncovered interior point
accepted_units.why_material: The first proof branch maps a persistent relative class into the physical pair, uses commutativity with the connecting homomorphism to retain nonzero boundary degree, and applies duality after removing a hypothetical uncovered point. The resulting vanishing contradiction converts an algebraic witness into a global coverage conclusion.
accepted_units.context_note: This is one branch of the sufficient coverage theorem and presupposes assumptions (A1)-(A6), the simplex-realization lemma, and connectedness away from the boundary. It is not a converse and contains no probabilistic claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The argument depends on relative homology, the exact pair map, the long exact sequence, and Alexander duality; the commutative diagram is flattened in normalization but is restated in prose.

accepted_units.title: An auxiliary scale and exactness eliminate the remaining proof branch
accepted_units.why_material: When the boundary degree vanishes, the proof factors the class through an intermediate scale, uses collar annihilation and exactness to lift it to absolute homology, then factors onward through a Cech complex whose top homology vanishes. Commutativity yields a contradiction with persistence, showing how an auxiliary representation can certify a fact without being computed.
accepted_units.context_note: The intermediate complex is a proof object only. The argument is deterministic, conditional on the boundary-collar assumptions and scale inequalities, and should not be mistaken for an implemented additional measurement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Exactness, the two commutative diagrams, dimension-specific scale constants, Cech factorization, and top-dimensional vanishing all matter; normalized diagrams and constants require source verification.

accepted_units.title: A rigorous certificate may be deliberately conservative and need not characterize success
accepted_units.why_material: The source explicitly separates sufficiency from necessity: poor scale choices can destroy the certificate, and actual coverage may hold even when the persistent class test fails. It also distinguishes an auxiliary object required by the proof from objects that must be computed in practice.
accepted_units.context_note: These are limitations of the theorem and proof architecture, not simulation-derived failure rates. They prevent treating a failed homology test as evidence of noncoverage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate. The limitation is conceptually robust, but examples depend on the chosen sensing, communication, and boundary scales.
